primary_claim: Finetuning LLMs on declarative descriptions of chatbot personas reduces the number of iterative finetuning steps needed to reach a given level of behaviour matching that persona, and increases self-identification with the correct persona, showing LLMs can perform cross-context abductive reasoning

effect.metric: iterative finetuning steps to reach threshold mean proportion of vowel-beginning words (~0.50)
effect.value: treatment GPT-4o reached the threshold after 4 iterations vs 7 for the control

contradicts_or_qualifies: Berglund et al. (2023) showed cross-context deduction/reward-hacking that relies on a trigger-keyword prompt pointing to the relevant declarative data; this work tests abductive inference of the relevant context without such a trigger keyword
stated_future_work: Identify whether LLMs reason deductively from abductively-inferred hypotheses, rather than relying purely on associations
Extend cross-context abduction experiments to more diverse behaviours, e.g. cognitive biases of preference data labelers
Test cross-context abduction where declarative facts are not present in recent finetuning/training data (e.g. via pretraining from scratch)
Prevent declarative data distribution leakage into iterative finetuning data to enable expert iteration and RLHF on open-source LLMs
limitations_stated: Results in experiment 2b are noisy, possibly due to catastrophic forgetting or mode collapse
Cross-context abduction tested for very few tasks
Declarative finetuning data induced a length bias in treatment model responses that invalidated some expert-iteration comparisons
Did not set/record a fixed random seed for the OpenAI finetuning API at the time of running experiments
quote: I show that finetuning LLMs on declarative data describing different personas reduces the number of iterative finetuning steps (a proxy for reinforcement learning) required to display behaviour sufficiently in line with one of the personas (Experiment 2a).
